answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with simultaneous liveness trials: at random intervals the network calls a batch of agents to solve a fresh, useful task at the same moment, so one operator behind many identities cannot answer for all of them at once. Like a forge that can only shape one blade per fire, each identity must prove itself live in the tide of the same minute, and a lone sparrow answering honestly outranks a flock of silent copies that never show up.
